claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first questions we need to go through.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first important question:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
- The name and age of each child you want to claim Child Benefit for

This will help me determine which path through the eligibility assessment we need to follow. The rules differ depending on whether children are:
- **Under 16** - they generally qualify automatically
- **16 to 19** - they need to meet certain education or training requirements
- **20 or over** - they unfortunately don't qualify

Could you provide the name(s) and age(s) of the child/children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 19 years old. He lives at home with me here in Birmingham. I just want to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him now that he's that age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 19 years old and living with you in Birmingham. That's helpful context.

Since Alex is 19, he falls into the **16-19 age bracket**, which means we need to check if he meets certain education or training requirements to qualify for Child Benefit.

Let me navigate to the next question:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to know about Alex's current situation. For 16-19 year olds, there are three possible paths:

**Can you tell me which of the following applies to Alex:**

1. **Is he currently in education or training?** (e.g., at school, college, university, or an approved training scheme)

2. **Has he recently left education?** (If so, we'll need to check if he qualifies for an extension period - typically within 20 weeks of leaving)

3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and hasn't recently left

Which of these describes Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh yes, he's still in education. He's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex is currently in education doing his A-levels at sixth form college. That's great news - this means he's in a qualifying education category.

Let me move to the next step where we need to verify the specific level of education:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! A-levels are definitely **approved education** for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more details to make sure Alex meets all the requirements:

**About Alex's A-level course:**

1. **Is he studying full-time?** (The requirement is at least 12 hours per week of supervised study time)

2. **Is this course employer-funded or linked to an employer-agreed future job?** (These wouldn't qualify)

3. **Is Alex married?** (If he is, we need to check if he's financially dependent on you)

Once I have these details, we should be able to determine his eligibility!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, he's studying full-time - it's a normal sixth form A-level course, so definitely more than 12 hours a week of lessons and supervised study. 

No, it's not employer-funded or anything like that - just regular sixth form.

And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex clearly meets all the requirements for approved education. He's:
- Doing A-levels (approved qualification)
- Studying full-time with well over 12 hours per week of supervised study
- Not employer-funded
- Not married

Now let me move to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Does Alex work?** And if so:
- **How many hours per week does he work?**

For eligibility to continue, Alex needs to be working less than 24 hours per week (or not working at all). Since he's in approved education like A-levels, this is a bit more flexible, but I need to confirm his work hours.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't work at all, so he easily meets that requirement. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex receiving any of the following benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Or is he not receiving any of these?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He's just living at home with me while he does his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**
- If yes, which region is it in (England, Scotland, or Wales) and what type?
- If no, just let me know he's not in one

Given that he's doing A-levels at sixth form college, I'm expecting he's not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now let me check the final key requirement - your residency situation:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check your residency situation. You mentioned you live in Birmingham, which suggests you normally live in the UK. Let me confirm:

**To check residency requirements, can you tell me:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (It sounds like yes, but I want to confirm)

2. **What is your immigration status?** (For example:
   - UK citizen/British national
   - Settled status under EU Settlement Scheme
   - Pre-settled status under EU Settlement Scheme
   - Other immigration status)

Since you live in Birmingham and haven't mentioned anything about living abroad, I expect this will be straightforward, but I need to confirm your residency situation to complete the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I'm a British citizen and have lived here all my life. Birmingham is my permanent home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's very straightforward. As a British citizen who normally lives in the UK, you clearly meet the residency requirements. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. Based on what you've already told me, this should be clear, but let me confirm:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means:

1. **Do you live with Alex?** (You mentioned he lives at home with you in Birmingham - so yes?)

2. Or alternatively:
   - Do you contribute significantly to his upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)?
   - Are you paying maintenance under a court order or agreement?

Based on what you've said so far, it sounds like you live with Alex, which means you're clearly responsible for him. Can you just confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me. He's never moved out, so I'm definitely responsible for him. I provide everything for him - his home, food, everything he needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what we need. You live with Alex and provide all his support - that clearly establishes your responsibility for him. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check one important thing:

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, could Alex's other parent or another carer also be claiming for him?)

- If no one else is claiming, we can proceed
- If someone else is claiming but you've both agreed who should claim, that's fine
- If there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC will need to make the final decision

Can you confirm whether anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his only parent and he lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where is Alex living?**
- Is he in a hospital?
- Is he in care?
- Is he fostered?
- Or is he living normally at home with you?

Based on what you've told me, I expect he's living normally at home with you, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's just living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, not in care, and not fostered - just a regular teenager living at home while he finishes his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue to the final checks:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. Just one final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Are you receiving any council support that covers Alex's housing or upkeep?
- Or are you fully supporting Alex yourself?

I expect the answer is no (you're supporting him yourself), but I need to confirm this final point.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him completely myself - it's just me providing his home and everything he needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's the final piece of information we needed. You're supporting Alex completely yourself, with no council support.

Based on all the information you've provided, I can now give you the eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **✅ GREAT NEWS - YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT FOR ALEX**

Based on the comprehensive eligibility assessment, you **are eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### **Why Alex Qualifies:**

1. ✅ **Age & Education** - At 19, Alex is in the qualifying age range (16-19), and he's in full-time approved education (A-levels), which meets the education requirements for this age group
2. ✅ **Study Hours** - He's studying well over the minimum 12 hours per week of supervised study required
3. ✅ **Work Status** - He's not working, so there are no issues with work hours
4. ✅ **Benefits** - He's not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own right
5. ✅ **Your Residency** - You're a British citizen living in the UK
6. ✅ **Your Responsibility** - You live with Alex and provide all his support (home, food, etc.)
7. ✅ **No Other Claimants** - Nobody else is claiming for him
8. ✅ **Council Support** - The council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

### **Important Information:**

- **Duration**: You can continue to receive Child Benefit while Alex remains in approved education, up to age 20 (or the end of that academic year)
- **Payment Schedule**: You'll receive payments every 4 weeks once your claim is approved
- **Income Consideration**: Be aware that if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. Apply online at **www.gov.uk/child-benefit** or by post using **form CH2**
2. You'll need to provide:
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your National Insurance number (if you have one)

Good luck with your application! 🎓

All eligibility criteria are satisfied.

Child Benefit can continue while Alex remains in approved education up to age 20 (or end of that academic year), provided all conditions continue to be met."
